note: Patches applied to a pinned sibling checkout before generation, so a module the compiler refuses to lower today can still ship. A patch here may only rewrite an expression into an equivalent the compiler does lower. It may NEVER change observable behavior -- absence, reference identity, equality, ordering, exception shape, task settlement -- because the generated header is then tested against the patched source, so a behavioral patch is a lie our own tests would certify. Each patch states the equivalence that makes it safe and the refusal it answers. The patch is applied after the pin integrity check and reverted when generation ends, so the checkout is only ever dirty inside one run. `baseCommit` pins the patch to the revision it was written against: a pin move that breaks the patch fails loudly instead of silently applying to different code.

patches.equivalence: The expression is unevaluated: no reference is dereferenced at runtime and no object is allocated, copied, cast, or observed. It recovers the same source member's C++ type from the object behind the carrier; the existing every-constraint-arm proof still decides whether the key may be emitted.
patches.verification: Focused backend fixtures require the carrier member spelling. Materials-only regeneration emits get_material_of_kind<T> through T->kind, all 24 package headers compile at -j2, and the native materials test instantiates match, mismatch, and null paths while asserting exact returned owner identity.
patches.whyNotUpstreamFirst: This is a backend representation defect at the pinned compiler revision and the target spelling follows directly from the reference carrier selected for generated interfaces; the request and focused reproduction accompany the carried patch.
patches.unblocks: @flighthq/materials getMaterialOfKind concrete discriminant instantiation and other dependent indexed accesses over generated interface carriers.
patches.expires: when dependent indexed access consults the selected C++ representation and reads generated interface members through their reference carrier.

The same Any value performs the same exact-type lookup, returns the same shared owner, and throws on the same mismatch; no cast, alternative selection, copy, or source behavior changes. The added disjunct widens only when the disambiguator is emitted, never what the recovery does.

patches.refusal: reading Error.name from an erased value requires both an instance flight::Error::name() const accessor
patches.rewrite: Lowers the two Error reads the runtime now answers: a typed `Error.name` becomes a call on the instance accessor, and an erased Error property read goes through the checked `flight::Any` Error view with the `instanceof Error` guard lowered to that view's own presence test. The refusal is retained only for an erased read the view cannot answer.
patches.equivalence: The emitted C++ reads the same object the source named: `name()` is virtual, so a RangeError held as an Error answers RangeError; `error_if()` recovers the boxed object with no copy and no second Error, and `has_value()` is true exactly when the value is an Error or a subclass, which is what `instanceof Error` tests. A value that is not an Error follows the same branch the source's else-branch would take, and `.value()` after the guard throws rather than reading an invented member. No reflection, no coercion, and no behavior change for any other type.
patches.whyNotUpstreamFirst: The runtime half landed at flight-cpp commit 48e4424 (instance accessor, reference-backed Error, checked Any view); this is the lowering that consumes it, and upstream has no newer commit than the pin.
patches.unblocks: the erased Error property reads in @flighthq/log and @flighthq/audio, plus the typed Error.name reads in @flighthq/log.
patches.expires: when upstream lowers Error.name to an instance accessor and erased Error reads through a checked projection of its own.

No member is invented and no field is added to `Error` or `Any`; a runtime that carries the member later earns the lowering, and this refusal then disappears with the patch.

patches.refusal: Object.assign requires one closed callable-object target and an exact compatible object literal source
patches.rewrite: Merges a class resolver's contribution into the accumulating format with a spread assignment instead of Object.assign, and lets the accumulator be reassigned.
patches.equivalence: Both forms copy the contribution's own enumerable properties onto the accumulator in the same order, so a later class still overrides an earlier one on a shared field and every untouched field keeps its previous value. The accumulator starts empty, is never aliased by a caller, and is returned as a fresh object either way; a null contribution still leaves it unchanged. No property is read, coerced, or dropped that the source did not already read.
patches.whyNotUpstreamFirst: A spread assignment is the ordinary target-neutral spelling for merging one object into another, and it states the result as a new object rather than an in-place mutation the emitter cannot witness.

patches.refusal: the emitter's runtime external symbol binding plan declares no type for IteratorResult or IteratorYieldResult, so the result of Map.keys().next() cannot cross into C++: naming IteratorResult<number> asks for a binding that does not exist, and leaving it inferred re-derives an anonymous structural row incompatible with the runtime IteratorResult carrier
patches.rewrite: Reads the first key by iterating runtime.lru.keys() with an immediate return, instead of calling next() and inspecting its done/value fields, so no iterator-result type is named or materialized at all.
patches.equivalence: Map preserves insertion order, so the first key the for-of yields is exactly the key the previous first next() returned; the body runs for that single key and returns true on it, and an empty map falls through to return false. The same lru.delete, _releaseGlyphBudget, entries.delete and bitmaps.delete calls run in the same order on the same key, the iterator is advanced once either way, and no value is copied, moved, or re-read.
patches.whyNotUpstreamFirst: Target-neutral: an immediate return from a first iteration is the ordinary idiom for 'take the first key', it keeps Flight's Map insertion-order contract, and it avoids both a missing binding and a use-site row.
patches.unblocks: Lets glyphAtlasEntry.ts emit without a new external binding, which in turn supplies setGlyphAtlasEntryGuard and getGlyphAtlasEntry to enable_glyph_atlas_guards.hpp and glyph_source.hpp.
patches.expires: when the runtime contract binds IteratorResult (and decides IteratorYieldResult), so the direct next() form lowers.
patches.replaces: the previous form of this patch, which annotated the next() result as IteratorResult<number>; that annotation is what began asking for the missing IteratorResult[type] binding

patches.refusal: reads of members on Map.get results go through a non-null assertion the emitter cannot carry: in _repackGlyphAtlas both the sort comparator's entry height reads and the loop's entry/bitmap width and height reads sit on absence-carrying storage with no present-value proof
patches.rewrite: Binds each Map.get result to a local, tests it explicitly, and only then reads members: the comparator falls back to the numeric key order when a key is absent, and the loop skips a codepoint whose entry or bitmap is missing.
patches.equivalence: Both Maps are written together, so while the atlas invariant holds every key yielded by entries.keys() has both an entry and a bitmap, and every guarded branch therefore takes the same path it took before: the comparator returns the identical height delta (entries carry the same heights, and the fallback only orders keys the original would have asserted present), and the loop performs the same placement, mutation and pixel write for the same codepoint in the same order. The only difference is on invariant violation, where TypeScript's assertion would dereference undefined and throw, while this skips that codepoint; no sequence of legal atlas operations reaches it.
patches.whyNotUpstreamFirst: Binding a Map result to a local and testing it is the ordinary way to write a presence-safe read; it keeps the source target-neutral and states the invariant in the code rather than in an assertion.
patches.unblocks: Removes the four unproven member reads that refuse glyphAtlasEntry.ts, so the module emits and supplies setGlyphAtlasEntryGuard and getGlyphAtlasEntry to enable_glyph_atlas_guards.hpp and glyph_source.hpp.
patches.expires: when a Map.get on absence-carrying storage carries a present-value proof from a preceding has()/assertion into later member reads.

patches.refusal: `x ??= y` whose target has a declared type with no absent member is emitted as the target alone, so the write disappears. An `unknown`/`any` target is carried as the erased `flight::Any`, whose nullishness is a runtime property of the value rather than of the type, so the no-op shortcut is unsound for exactly that carrier: `failure ??= error;` in a catch body emits a bare `failure;`, the first failure is never recorded, and the `if (failure !== null) throw failure;` that follows can never fire -- a failed teardown becomes indistinguishable from a successful one. Measured in `@flighthq/power`'s `destroyPowerKeepAwake` and `detachPower`; the same construct first appears in `particleEmitterSignals.ts`, whose record-typed target took a different lowering lane and so did not show it.
patches.rewrite: One branch of the assignment lowering: a `??=` target whose declared type has no absent member AND whose C++ carrier is the erased `flight::Any` (IR type kind `unknown`) now lowers to the guarded assignment `([&]() { auto&& assignment_target = LEFT; if (assignment_target.is_nullish()) assignment_target = RIGHT; return assignment_target; }())`, using the carrier's own loose nullish test. A target whose carrier cannot hold a nullish value -- a `number` target's `double` -- keeps the no-op, and a target carried as an optional keeps `emitLogicalAssignmentCpp`. Catch breadth is deliberately untouched: the handler remains `catch (const std::exception&)`, which is a separate open defect (docs/compiler-requests/catch-handler-breadth-attempt-all.md).
patches.equivalence: The old shortcut returned the target unmodified, which is the correct lowering only where the carrier cannot hold null or undefined; that is now the only case that keeps it. Where the carrier is the erased `flight::Any`, the emitted code records the right-hand side exactly when JavaScript would, and the loose `is_nullish()` matches `??=`'s rule that null and undefined both assign rather than either strict half. An assignment still evaluates to the target's value, the condition is evaluated once per evaluation, a target that already holds a value is left alone -- which is what retains the FIRST failure across later iterations -- and no absent member, no refusal, and no runtime capability is invented.
patches.verification: New `cppNullishAssignmentStatement.test.ts`, 4 pass: the `??=` statement inside a catch body keeps a conditional write and is no longer a bare target; the same holds in an expression position; the guard is the loose `is_nullish()`, not either strict half; and a number target keeps the no-op. Reverting the branch fails 3 of those 4 and leaves the number-target case passing. `cppCompilerBackend.test.ts` reports the same 24 failures before and after the change (pre-existing at this base, none of them this shape), so the branch adds no regression and removes none. The companion patch compiler-catch-recorded-slot-carrier claims the catch-recorded slot, so this test's fixtures were retargeted to shapes it does not claim; the pair was re-verified together: all 40 compiler patches apply in manifest order over a clean checkout and both backend test files pass 9/9.
patches.unblocks: `@flighthq/power`'s attempt-all teardown: `destroyPowerKeepAwake` and `detachPower` promise in their own source comment to rethrow the first failure once the siblings have run, which their emitted bodies could not do. Regenerating the package's slice with this patch is what the unit's second half measures; the behaviour left unasserted there is the catch-breadth half, which stays open.
patches.expires: when the emitter distinguishes a carrier that cannot hold a nullish value from one whose value decides it without the declared-absence-member test.
patches.whyNotUpstreamFirst: The defect is one condition in the pinned backend's assignment lowering that mis-classifies an erased carrier, not a missing contract, so it needs no new runtime capability and no new evidence channel -- the carrier's own `is_nullish()` already exists and is already used elsewhere in the same file. A narrow versioned patch repairs the pinned implementation, and the focused backend test it carries is the regression guard for the exact shape.

patches.refusal: an `unknown` slot that a catch/attempt-all pattern records into is carried as `std::exception_ptr` only when it has NO initializer, records with `=` and is read nowhere but its record and its rethrow. `let failure: unknown = null;` therefore stays on the erased `flight::Any` path, which cannot hold a caught exception at all: with the record lowering in place the emitted assignment does not compile. The same source shape without the initializer lowers correctly, so the initializer alone decides whether the caught value is representable.
patches.rewrite: Three conditions in the exception-slot election and two lanes that must agree with it. The candidate now admits an initializer that is a nullish literal (`null`/`undefined`, which is the same 'no failure recorded yet' an empty `std::exception_ptr` means), a `??=` whose right side is a catch binding counts as a recording assignment rather than an invalid one, and a nullish presence test of the slot counts as a permitted reference. The record lane lowers `slot ??= caught` to `if (!slot) slot = std::current_exception();`, which keeps the FIRST failure, and the presence-test lane lowers the slot's nullish test to pointer emptiness for either sentinel. Everything else stays: a slot initialized to a non-nullish value, recorded from anything but a catch binding, never rethrown, or read for its value rather than its presence keeps the erased carrier.
patches.equivalence: An empty `std::exception_ptr` and the source's `null` initializer are the same state -- 'nothing recorded yet' -- so admitting the initializer changes which carrier is chosen, not what the program means; the `??=` guard assigns exactly when the slot is empty, which is `??=`'s rule for this carrier and is what retains the first failure; and both sentinels answer the same way because the slot only ever holds either nothing or a recorded exception. Reference counting still requires every read of the slot to be a record, the rethrow, or the presence test, so a slot whose *value* other code consumes is untouched, and the catch handler itself is not changed in any way: it stays `catch (const std::exception&)`, so non-class throws still escape a continuing handler, which remains the separate open defect.
patches.verification: New `cppCatchRecordedSlotCarrier.test.ts`, 5 pass: the attempt-all slot takes `std::exception_ptr`, records once through the guarded `current_exception()`, is tested as pointer emptiness rather than through the erased carrier, and rethrows through `std::rethrow_exception`; and three controls keep `flight::Any` -- an ordinary `unknown` slot assigned a plain value, a slot recorded but never rethrown, and a slot read for its value as well as its presence. Running the same file against the record-lowering patch alone fails 2 of those 5 (the carrier and the presence test) and passes the three controls. `cppCompilerBackend.test.ts` reports the same 24 failures with both patches as it does with the record patch alone and with neither (pre-existing at this base). It also retargets the fixtures of compiler-nullish-assignment-statement-in-catch, whose own fixture is a catch-recorded slot this patch now claims; verified together by applying all 40 compiler patches in manifest order to a clean checkout (0 failures) and running both backend test files there, 9/9.
patches.unblocks: Regenerating `@flighthq/power` package-scoped with both patches: `destroyPowerKeepAwake` and `detachPower` compile, record the first failure of an attempt-all teardown, and rethrow it -- the behaviour their source comments promise. With the record patch alone the module does not compile at all, so the two patches are a pair.
patches.expires: when the election asks what the slot's carrier must be able to hold rather than how the source happened to spell its initializer, record, and reads.
patches.whyNotUpstreamFirst: The election is a closed-shape rule in the pinned backend with its own stated intent in a comment -- it protects ordinary unknown storage from the exception carrier -- and these three conditions are that intent spelled more precisely, not a new contract: the carrier, the record and the rethrow it needs all already exist. A narrow versioned patch with focused controls is the smallest change that lets the source's own attempt-all shape lower, and the controls are what keep the rule from widening.

patches.refusal: a `catch (error)` whose body only reifies the caught value -- the attempt-all teardown that records the first failure and rethrows it after the siblings -- is emitted as `catch (const std::exception& error)`. A thrown value that is not a class therefore never reaches the handler: it escapes, the loop is skipped, and the remaining obligations are stranded. C++ has a value channel for this (`throw 42`), and `std::current_exception()` reifies any thrown value, so the narrow binding is not a representation limit -- it is a binding the body does not need.
patches.rewrite: In the catch-clause emission, a handler whose binding is referenced ONLY as the right side of a record into a slot carried as `std::exception_ptr` -- the record the exception-carrier patch lowers to `std::current_exception()`, which never mentions the binding -- is emitted as `catch (...)`. A handler that reads the value (a member, an argument, a direct rethrow) keeps `catch (const std::exception& name)`, because C++ cannot name a non-class caught value at all; that is the boundary this lowering stops at, and staying narrow there is deliberate. A handler with no binding is unchanged (`catch (...)` already).
patches.equivalence: The value rethrown is the value caught, for every thrown type: `std::rethrow_exception` rethrows the same object a class throw produced -- a caller catching `flight::Error` sees exactly what it saw before -- and rethrows the same `int` a primitive throw produced, which the narrow handler could not deliver at all. The record is still `std::current_exception()` and the rethrow is still `std::rethrow_exception`, so first-failure retention is unchanged, and the attempt-all loop now runs its siblings for a non-class throw instead of being skipped by it. Nothing is boxed into a carrier it was not: the widening is exactly 'catch everything, keep the exception pointer', and where that is not faithful the handler is left narrow.
patches.verification: New `cppCatchHandlerBreadth.test.ts`, 4 pass: the reify-only attempt-all handler is `catch (...)` with the exception-pointer record and rethrow; a handler that rethrows the binding directly and one that records it into a NON-exception slot both keep the narrow `catch (const std::exception& error)`; and a binding-less handler is unchanged. Neutralising the condition fails the first case and leaves the three boundary controls passing. Applied with the other compiler patches in manifest order, all 41 apply and the three backend test files pass 13/13; the behavioural proof for a primitive throw is in `@flighthq/power`'s native test.
patches.unblocks: `@flighthq/power`'s attempt-all teardown is faithful for every thrown value it can be given: with a provider whose destroy throws a number, the sibling is still attempted and the caller catches that same number, where the narrow handler skipped the sibling and the value escaped.
patches.expires: when the emitter can name a non-class caught value where the source reads it, at which point the narrow form is never needed.
patches.whyNotUpstreamFirst: The narrow form is a binding choice in the catch-clause emission, not a missing contract: the value channel (`catch (...)`, `std::current_exception()`, `std::rethrow_exception`) is already used elsewhere in the same file and already lowered for the binding-less handler. The patch narrows exactly which handlers may keep the binding, and its controls pin the boundary.

In JavaScript an omitted argument and an explicit undefined are the same value, and the body only tests `parentRuntime ? ... : 0`, so every observable result is unchanged. This NARROWS the exported TypeScript/C++ signature: a one-argument call no longer type-checks. No caller in the SDK makes one; a consumer that does must pass undefined.
patches.whyNotUpstreamFirst: The emitter both writes the default on the definition and enters this function through an include cycle; upstream needs to emit default arguments on a leading declaration (as it did at 7e2fc7d). patches.refusal: silent miscompilation, measured natively: accumulateForces' string switch lowers to an if/else chain inside the force loop, and the `if (dist <= 1e-6) break;` / `if (mag === 0) break;` early exits of AttractorForce and VortexForce are copied through as C++ `break`, which leaves the force loop instead of the case -- so a force outside its radius, or sitting on the particle, discards every later force for that particle (docs/compiler-requests/switch-case-break-exits-enclosing-loop.md)

patches.equivalence: In the source each `break` ends the case with nothing after it executed; the guards enclose exactly the statements after each `break` and test the negated condition (`dist > 1e-6` for `dist <= 1e-6`, including NaN, which fails both; `mag !== 0` for `mag === 0`), so the same accumulations happen in the same order for every input, and the loop continues to the next force as the switch's `break` does.
patches.verification: Guarded pkg:generate of @flighthq/particles at a627849, then pkg:compile: 13/13 headers compile; the generated_particles CTest pins an out-of-radius attractor, a zero-distance attractor and a zero-distance vortex each followed by a wind force that still applies.
patches.whyNotUpstreamFirst: The defect is the emitter lowering a nested switch `break` as a loop `break` (docs/compiler-requests/switch-case-break-exits-enclosing-loop.md); the fix belongs in the compiler and is general. This keeps particle forces correct until it lands.
patches.unblocks: Correct accumulateForces for force lists where an attractor or vortex exits early; no header-count change.
patches.expires: when a `break` nested inside a lowered switch case ends only that case.

patches.refusal: deduction compares a callee's `Readonly<Signal<T>>` parameter against the caller's `Signal<() => void>` argument by name, finds `Readonly` against `Signal`, and gives up, so the callee's own type parameter reaches emission unsubstituted and the call site spells an undeclared `Signal<T>`

patches.equivalence: `Readonly<T>` is a view over the same value, not a second owner: a readonly structural parameter receives the concrete reference itself, which is what `getCppStructuralProjectionRowCpp` already records when it answers a `readonly` row for `Readonly`, and what the emitted `StructuralRef<RowReadonly<RowOf<Ref<T>>>>` says. The patch changes which type argument is named, never which value is passed: the emitted cast, the row, the reference, and the callee are the same object graph, and no runtime representation, absence, equality, ordering, or settlement rule is touched. Only `Readonly` is unwrapped -- `NoInfer`, unions, and every other ambient wrapper keep the comparison they had -- and an argument whose owner differs from the parameter's still fails deduction, so no substitution is invented.
patches.verification: Two-module fixture (helper imported from its package, since an ambient `declare function` refuses earlier) asserts the emitted row names `Signal<std::function<void()>>` and contains no `Signal<T>`; the negative fixture asserts a `Readonly<Signal<T>>` parameter is not filled from an `Emitter<() => void>` argument. The substituted pair syntax-checks with the pinned C++ toolchain. The C++ backend suite is unchanged by the patch: 24 failures before and after (all pre-existing in this checkout), 1461 -> 1463 passing, 32 -> 33 skipped.
patches.whyNotUpstreamFirst: The representation layer already treats `Readonly<T>` and `T` as one value and deduces across them elsewhere; this makes type-parameter deduction agree with it. Upstream has no newer commit than the pin.
patches.unblocks: `@flighthq/power` compiles instead of failing all three of its headers on `use of undeclared identifier 'T'`; `@flighthq/preferences` reaches the same helper through `storage.ts`.
patches.expires: when upstream deduces a generic parameter through a readonly view from argument evidence.

patches.refusal: a local initialized straight from a bound host call is declared from the library signature's numeric token, so `const id = setInterval(tick, ms)` emits `const double id = host::set_interval(tick, ms)` -- the handle placed in a double

The patch changes which type the local is declared as, not which value it holds: the same call, the same handle, the same identity reaching the matching clearInterval. It applies only to a bare primitive declared type that came from the callee's own library signature, on a call the emitter resolved through the binding table; a declared union keeps its existing path and any other declared type still refuses as `cpp-external-binding-missing-source-type-evidence`, so no disagreement is papered over and no carrier is invented where a binding names none.

Package typecheck and oxfmt clean.

patches.refusal: the create-result union names its failure arm as an inline `Entity & Exclude<...>` while tray.ts builds that value from a second inline intersection, so the arm and the value are sibling C++ structs and the value cannot enter its own arm; the tray runtime is allocated as an EntityRuntime and asserted to a source-local TrayRuntime, which the emitter cannot follow between two unrelated owners

Naming them adds no member and widens none. The narrowed entity slot says what the module already asserted on every read -- that a tray's runtime is a `TrayRuntime` -- and it is the shape @flighthq/types already gives Node, where the runtime sits beside the entity and the slot is narrowed there. The runtime literal carries the same fields with the same values the prior allocate-then-assign produced, including `binding: null`; initialization, state transitions, animation timing, release bookkeeping and identity are unchanged, and no object is copied, cast at runtime or replaced.

patches.unblocks: @flighthq/tray: ten refused functions across `cpp-intersection-member-shapeless`, `cpp-uninitialized-variable-missing-type-evidence` and `cpp-reference-assertion-without-heritage`, and the four tray headers that fail to compile on the erased runtime accessor.
patches.expires: when the compiler joins an intersection arm to the value that fills it and can read an entity's runtime slot through an owner it does not declare, or Flight names the arm and narrows the slot upstream.

patches.refusal: uncompilable emission, not a refusal: after `request.body !== undefined` narrows an optional member typed `string | ArrayBuffer | ArrayBufferView | null`, the following `request.body !== null` reads the projected inner value (`row_get<"body">(request).value()`) and applies the two-level storage test to it, calling has_value() on the payload std::variant (net.hpp:52)

For `!== null` the storage test answers true for undefined, false for null and true for a present value, which is the source semantics. Short-circuit evaluation keeps the earlier `!== undefined` guard in force, so narrowing is supplied by control flow rather than by projecting the operand. Un-narrowed reads, plain-payload members and every other presence lane emit exactly what they did before. No absence, identity, equality, ordering, exception or settlement behavior changes; the code it replaces did not compile.

Two-module repro with a profile-bound ArrayBufferView arm: `!== undefined && !== null` and `=== undefined || === null` both test the storage. Controls: an un-narrowed strict test, a loose `!= null`, and a plain `string | number[]` payload are unchanged. Without the rewrite the two narrowed cases fail and the controls pass. compiler-backend-cpp suite: the same 46 pre-existing failures by name with and without the patch, 1699 passing with it.
patches.whyNotUpstreamFirst: The projection appears only when a payload arm is a profile-bound runtime type, which exists only through this repository's binding profiles; upstream receives the request with the fixture.
patches.unblocks: @flighthq/net: the only compile error in its five headers at a627849 (net.hpp, through which _internal_index, contract and enable_net_guards fail).
patches.expires: when upstream emits presence tests on narrowed optional-nullable members against their storage (docs/compiler-requests/nested-nullable-property-narrowed-null-test.md).

''` fallback is unreachable, and `channels` is non-empty exactly when `numberOfChannels > 0`, which the early return now tests directly before the element is named. No value is copied, no absence is invented, and no member is read that the source did not already read.

patches.refusal: object-literal diagnostic details are emitted as a brace initializer that cannot cross both Record and optional<Record> construction boundaries (no matching constructor for std::optional<flight::Record<flight::String, std::variant<bool, double, flight::String>>>)

patches.refusal: silent miscompilation, not a refusal: a null or undefined comparison of a runtime array element (`slots[i] !== null`) is emitted as `slots.get(i).has_value()`. Array::get answers std::optional around the element's own storage, so that tests the index-miss layer only: a null element of a (T | null)[] reads as present, and a miss reads as null. @flighthq/signals therefore counts tombstoned slots as live and never compacts them.
patches.rewrite: emitCppPresenceTestCpp gains a lane for an element read through a runtime array, written directly or retained by an immutable array-element binding (which keeps the same `get` carrier). It inspects the carrier in the order the comparison asks: the outer layer is the index miss JavaScript reads as undefined; when the element type stores null (or undefined) as optional absence, the inner layer is that sentinel. An element type with no absence of its own has only the outer layer, so a strict null test is type-decided. The operand is evaluated once in every form. RegExpExecArray captures and typed arrays keep their own lanes. A binding's declaration owns its storage and an emission repair may flatten a declared single-absence binding to one layer (signals-flatten-generic-slot-read, animation-state-machine-flatten-channel-index-read), so a binding's test dispatches at compile time on the carrier it actually has, inside a generic lambda so the branch not taken is never instantiated.
patches.equivalence: For s: (T | null)[], JavaScript's s[i] is undefined on a miss, null on a null element, and the value otherwise. The emitted tests are exactly: !== null is miss or present; === null is in range and null; != null is in range and present; == null is miss or null; !== undefined is in range; === undefined is a miss. For (T | undefined)[] both layers mean undefined and strict null is false. For an element with no absence, strict null is constant and the rest test the miss. Checked against node on 90 cells (6 operators x direct read, bound local, null-element, undefined-element, callable-element and plain arrays x in-range null, in-range present, out of range): all match.

The repair-flattened binding form compiles for a concrete payload in non-template code and for a generic std::function payload, and answers correctly. compiler-backend-cpp suite: the same 46 pre-existing failures by name with and without the patch, 1724 passing with it. Natively: @flighthq/signals regenerated package-scoped; the three tombstone cases in tests/generated_signals_test.cpp are asserted and pass.

patches.rewrite: Lowers the test onto the operand's carrier through ONE runtime question, `flight::union_kind_if`, and routes the projection the guard proves through its throwing twin `flight::union_kind_or_throw`. The question is a compile-time walk of the carrier (optional, variant, or a bare erased value): an alternative of the target's own type answers with a pointer into the carrier, an `Any` alternative is asked through its checked external view, and anything else -- a string, an absence, an `Any` holding another type -- answers null without throwing. An operand with no recorded type, a union that neither names the target nor carries the erased arm, a target naming a source class or an unbound ambient, and a reference-shaped target (which has no stable view out of the erased carrier) each refuse by rule.
patches.equivalence: The guard and the projection ask the same question of the same carrier, so the guard can never admit a value the projection cannot produce -- which is what makes a projection without the proof behind it the only way the throwing twin can fire, and that is a compiler defect rather than a source-observable failure (`std::logic_error`, never a `flight::Error` a source `catch` could take for an application failure). The answer is a pointer INTO the carrier: the object that was there, never a copy, so reference identity survives. Answering false without throwing for a string, an absence, or an `Any` holding another type is the source's own answer for a value its guard rejected. Where the union has no erased arm the projection stays on the slot the source's alternative holds, so no package's emitted code moves for a union that could not reach one.

patches.rewrite: The backend carries what its own lowering already proved. A lowered `instanceof` guard records, for the branch it controls, the alternative it named for the path it tested -- the emitted `flight::union_kind_if` names both -- and a read of that same path inside the branch is emitted as that question's throwing twin, from the SAME carrier expansion. No alias is resolved a second time and no type reference is materialized that the module never wrote. The proof's lifetime is TypeScript's: a write to the path or to any prefix withdraws it before the statement that writes it is even emitted (an assignment target is a write, not a read, and a projection onto an lvalue is not C++); a call withdraws it for the statements AFTER it, because a property narrowing is invalidated at any call while a read inside the call's own statement is evaluated before it runs; and it never leaves the branch that proves it. A read the semantic layer's own proof already reaches is left to that proof, so nothing is projected twice.
patches.equivalence: The read is emitted from the guard's own proof, so the two cannot disagree: the projection is the throwing twin of the test that admitted the branch, over the same carrier expression. Its answer is a reference INTO that carrier, so the value is the one that was there and not a copy, and a divergence -- a projection emitted where the guard did not hold -- is a std::logic_error rather than a value the source could have observed. The lifetime rules are the ones the source language already has for a property narrowing, and each of them is a withdrawal rather than an invention: where the proof is gone the read is emitted exactly as it was before this patch.

patches.refusal: `if (pass.encoder !== null) { pass.encoder.end(); }` on a member of external type (`encoder: GPURenderPassEncoder | null`) is refused as cpp-member-projection-without-present-storage. The lowering's program erases an unresolved external type to `any`, and that also erases the `| null` beside it, so the checker's flow narrowing of the `binding.member` path is invisible. Binding references already recover the narrowing syntactically; member paths did not. This refuses beginWgpuRenderPass, endWgpuRenderPass and suspendWgpuRenderPass in render_wgpu/wgpu_render_pass.hpp.
patches.rewrite: getTypeScriptAccessPresence gains a closed syntactic fallback that applies only when the checker's member type is erased to `any`. A `binding.member` read is narrowedPresent when an enclosing guard excludes every absent kind named by the member's own declaration (`| null`, `| undefined`, `?`). The accepted guards are an if/else branch, `&&`/`||`, a conditional, or a preceding `if (absent) return/throw/break/continue` sibling. A strict test proves presence only when it names the declaration's single absent kind; the loose test covers both. Any write to the member or to its receiver binding between the guard and the read, or anywhere in an enclosing loop, withdraws the proof. A write target is never narrowed, so `binding.member = null` still clears the storage. Checker queries are made only after a purely syntactic precondition finds a matching guard spelling.

patches.equivalence: `in` asks whether the property exists on the object or its prototype chain.
